decisions.reason: As a close-to-core cardboard display variant that was still promoted a year after launch, it likely met a satisfactory aspiration level and a large firm has enough slack to retain it.
This pegboard-backed display fits the established offer and can serve specific customer needs, so absent clear signs of underperformance management would usually keep it.
Although it is somewhat generic and may overlap with other quarter-pallet formats, it is still near the core business and likely cheap for a large producer to carry unless results clearly disappoint.
The eighth-pallet format broadens the firm's standard retail display range with limited additional organisational burden, making retention more likely than withdrawal.

Because the wooden pallet sits further from the firm's paper-based core and likely uses less aligned resources, management would be more willing to reallocate capacity if its results were only modest in a flat market.

This media-focused quarter-pallet display is close to the core but more niche, so if demand has not clearly met aspirations the firm is likely to shift resources back to stronger standard display lines or new developments.
